text:
sara-support: Heads up — multiple customers reporting their console hourly usage is missing for 03:00–06:00 UTC. Started seeing alerts ~06:15 UTC. Screenshots show empty rows in the hourly view for several tenants. :warning:
devops-jay: looking now, can you paste a tenant id and link to a sample dashboard?
sara-support: tenant acme-corp (tenant_id: t_acme_42). dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/t_acme_42/usage?range=last24h
priya-ps: got a ticket open, customers are worried about billing visibility — flagging for priority. :eyes:
ingest-bot: Incident detected: hourly-rollup-worker lag spike at 2026-03-17T03:12:00Z. Kafka consumer group "hourly-rollup-v2" lag increased from 0 to 1.2M messages over 00:30.
devops-jay: ingest-bot shows consumer lag during backfill window — any running backfills? @data-eng-mel?
data-eng-mel: yes, we kicked a schema-swap backfill for partitioned rollups to reconcile new column names at 02:50 UTC. It should be non-blocking but maybe it overloaded the workers.
sara-support: customers report the missing hours are specifically the 03:00 and 04:00 buckets, 05:00 partially present.
data-eng-mel: possible explanation: backfill used the same consumer group id which bumped offsets; when backfill finished it rewound some checkpoints. We'll check consumer offsets and rehydrate queue.
devops-jay: running quick consumer-groups check now: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group hourly-rollup-v2`
devops-jay: output: PARTITION 0 offset=12345678 logEnd=13567890 lag=121222 (similar across partitions).
priya-ps: is the lag explain the missing rows? or are they just delayed? customers want ETA to see the hours return.
data-eng-mel: if lag is large, the rollup job hasn't processed the messages, so hours will be delayed. We need to avoid duplicate ingestion when we reprocess.
sara-support: any immediate mitigation? rollback?
data-eng-mel: mitigation plan: 1) pause non-critical backfill jobs, 2) scale hourly-rollup workers by +2 instances, 3) run targeted reprocess for affected tenant windows, 4) verify console queries.
ingest-bot: Backfill job id bf_20260317_schema_swap started 2026-03-17T02:50:12Z, pods: 4, current progress: 94%.
devops-jay: scaling workers now — applying deployment patch to hourly-rollup v2: replicas 3 -> 5.
devops-jay: pods coming up, CPU spike normalized.
data-eng-mel: running diagnostic SQL to check raw events and rollups for acme-corp: ```
-- check raw events count
select hour_bucket, count(*) from events.raw where tenant_id='t_acme_42' and ts >= '2026-03-17 02:00:00' and ts < '2026-03-17 07:00:00' group by hour_bucket order by hour_bucket;

-- check hourly rollups
select hour_bucket, count(*) from analytics.hourly_rollups where tenant_id='t_acme_42' and hour_bucket between '2026-03-17 02:00:00' and '2026-03-17 07:00:00' group by hour_bucket order by hour_bucket;
```
data-eng-mel: raw events are present for each hour; rollups missing for 03:00 & 04:00. Confirms processing gap.
sara-support: customers asking for repro steps — can we reproduce in staging?
data-eng-mel: yes reproduce by running the schema-swap backfill against staging while running a medium load on hourly-rollup consumer. I'll capture offsets.
priya-ps: expected ETA to restore console visibility?
data-eng-mel: with scaled workers we should clear the backlog in ~20–40 minutes depending on message size. Then run a targeted reprocess for those hour windows to catch any duplicates.
devops-jay: clearing lag — consumer lag dropped from 1.2M -> 120k in 10m after scale.
sara-support: telling customers estimated 45m for full visibility, will update.
priya-ps: log the outage for billing reconciliation — may need to exclude gap window from automated invoices if not restored by EOD.
data-eng-mel: action item: run reprocess script `scripts/reprocess_hours.sh t_acme_42 2026-03-17T03:00Z 2026-03-17T05:00Z` once lag < 10k. Will tag @devops-jay for a dry run in staging first.
devops-jay: will confirm once the reprocess completes in staging.
ingest-bot: consumer group hourly-rollup-v2 lag at 2026-03-17T06:05:00Z: 8,912.
data-eng-mel: initiating reprocess now (dry run mode) — checking dedupe keys and idempotency.
data-eng-mel: dry run shows 03:00 & 04:00 batches would insert ~4k rows each, no id collision expected.
sara-support: customers updated: they appreciate the ETA, asked for a postmortem.
priya-ps: assign postmortem to data-eng with SLO reviewer, include root cause: backfill using live consumer group + insufficient worker headroom.
data-eng-mel: noted. Will create postmortem checklist and propose safeguards: namespace isolation for backfills, consumer-group renaming, backfill rate limits, automated worker scale-up on high lag.
sara-support: Thanks team. Please ping when console shows restored hours so I can close tickets. :thumbsup:
